rationale: Requires intermediate representations to pass between stages without modification, which is data integrity.
Signature validation confirms the message origin (Authenticity, Integrity per signature rule) and the signer's identity must stay hidden from the controller (privacy).
Encrypting radar records so unauthorised readers cannot interpret them is confidentiality.
Restricts modification of bookmarks and form entries to the owner (Integrity) who must be verified in the session (Authenticity).
Admits a customer only after identifier and credential are validated, which is authentication.
Verifies analyst identity through certificate validation at login.
Verifies supplied credentials against user records before access, which is authentication.
A cryptographic signature on load records is used to detect later changes to the amount, i.e. integrity.
Credential reset for a registered developer via a link to the email on file concerns establishing identity and credentials.
Requires proprietary parameters to arrive encrypted and rejects them otherwise, protecting them from disclosure.
Checksum verification refusing compilation when components were modified is integrity of programs; no attack is named.
Protects encryption keys in a hardware key store so other applications cannot read them.
Reacts to a re-sent already-honoured licence grant, i.e. a replay, by aborting the job.
A hash on the stored balance with refusal on mismatch detects alteration of data.
Validates metadata ranges and rejects duplicate identifiers, which is data validity and coherence checking.
Encrypted transmission so intermediaries cannot read submitted values is confidentiality.
Hash comparison before release blocks payment of altered payslip batches, an integrity check.
Per-module grants of who may view and who may alter content cover both read and modify access control.
Detects and blocks malicious script injection while keeping simulations operating during the attempt.
Removes user names, paths and source snippets from crash reports to avoid disclosing sensitive data.
Guarantees matching debit and credit amounts and rejects inconsistent entries, which is data accuracy and coherence.
Purges intermediate customer data so later users cannot read it.
Dashboard access is granted only after the controller confirms the resident's identity.
Recomputes ledger checksum after rollback and keeps the entry unchanged, preserving data consistency.
Public-key encryption conceals session keys during distribution, protecting them from disclosure.
Rejects repeated crafted inputs meant to exhaust a service and alerts the administrator, resisting an attack.
Requires proof of profile ownership through a verified credential before restoring data, which is authentication.
Validates accuracy of clinical entries and rejects injected or manipulated entries that try to bypass checks.
Requires the cardholder's correct PIN before authorising a payment, which is authentication.
Detects an attacker's resubmitted (replayed) assertion and terminates the session and clears authenticated state.
A keyed authentication tag on each command detects alteration and verifies the paired hub as the origin.
Requires sign-in with an enrolled account and valid credential, which is authentication.
Discards stale-timestamp commands so recorded commands cannot be replayed to operate a lock.
Informs whether imported data has a verifiable source stamp confirming the provider's identity, i.e. origin authenticity.
Erases personal and payment data from temporary storage after timeout, protecting it from disclosure.
Digest comparison detects a modified source file before compilation.
Encrypts sensor and camera payloads so only the paired app can read them.
Prevents partially updated records and limits modification to users with an edit role.
A cryptographic checksum on the balance detects corruption or tampering of stored data.
